---
title: "Changelog"
---

Notable changes to JackMoebius.

Format: [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Versions 0.x cover the
initial development phase (before commercialization).

## 1.0.0 — first commercial release

JackMoebius is now a commercial product: a **14-day free trial**, then a one-time
license unlocks it for good — all updates included. This release also brings a
smoother onboarding and UX polish gathered since 0.13.

**Added**

- **14-day free trial**, then activate a license to keep routing. Activate in
  JackMate, or with `jackmoebius license activate`.
- Guided post-purchase onboarding and a GUI-first activation guide. JackMate — the
  free JACK patchbay & manager — is installed alongside JackMoebius (optional) and
  is the recommended way to drive it.

**Known limitations**

- **Zoom is not compatible.** Zoom rejects virtual audio devices on macOS (even via
  an Aggregate Device), so it is skipped by default. Every other tested app —
  Microsoft Teams, Audacity, OBS, browsers… — works normally.

## 0.13.2 — 2026-07-12

**Added**

- The bundled command-line tool can report the trial status offline (without a
  running daemon), so a front-end can show the days remaining at any time.

## 0.13.1 — 2026-07-12

Internal groundwork for the upcoming trial and license system. No change to how
JackMoebius works today — nothing is gated.

## 0.13.0 — 2026-07-11

**Added**

- **Signed and notarized by Apple.** The installer is code-signed and notarized, so
  it installs cleanly with no Gatekeeper warnings.
- The license agreement is shown during installation.

**Changed**

- In System Settings ▸ Login Items & Extensions, the background item is now clearly
  labeled **JackMoebius**.

## 0.12.3 — 2026-07-07

**Added**

- The daemon and CLI report the running build: a `jackmoebius --version` banner and a
  `version` field in the `status` reply, so a front-end can display and verify the
  installed version.
- Shell completion for the `version` subcommand.

## 0.12.2 — 2026-07-07

**Added**

- **Event-driven routing (step 2):** per-process CoreAudio device listeners emit
  fine-grained `routing_changed` events, so routing status stays live with no polling.

**Fixed**

- Reliable capture eligibility for multi-process apps — apps that play from helper
  processes (browsers, etc.) are now detected correctly.

## 0.12.1 — 2026-07-07

**Changed**

- The `apps` table is aligned, and channel ranges are shown compactly (e.g. `10->25`).

**Fixed**

- The daemon is launched through launchd rather than spawned as a child process (which
  broke JACK when started from the GUI).

## 0.12.0 — 2026-07-06

**Added**

- **Event-driven status (step 1):** a persistent `subscribe` channel over the IPC socket
  pushes invalidation events (exposure, apps, routing, master, JACK, stopping). A
  front-end stays in sync without polling and detects a daemon exit instantly.

## 0.11.3 — 2026-07-02

**Added**

- On a routing mismatch, the JACK listings name the device currently in use
  (`current_device` / `current_device_uid`), for a guided message in the GUI — both
  output and input directions.

## 0.11.2 — 2026-07-02

**Added**

- `status` reports per-direction exposed-box counts (`exposed_out` / `exposed_in`) so a
  front-end can gate its polling.

## 0.11.1 — 2026-06-26

**Added**

- Shell completion for the `blacklist` subcommand.

**Fixed**

- Per-app audio status is aggregated across an app's helper processes (so a browser
  playing from a helper reads as active), and listings show friendly names.

## 0.11.0 — 2026-06-26

**Added**

- **User blacklist:** apps you never want proposed for routing — hidden from `add` and
  from the app selector — with CLI management.

## 0.10.1 — 2026-06-26

**Added**

- The master box carries `org.jackmoebius.master` metadata so a front-end can recognise it.

## 0.10.0 — 2026-06-25

**Added**

- Symmetric `apps` IPC — independent input/output state per app.
- **Universal driver** (Intel + Apple Silicon).

**Changed**

- Per-app volume matches macOS's square-root volume taper.

**Fixed**

- The `jack_list_in` mirror.

## 0.9.0 — 2026-06-22 — First packaged version

The first formally versioned build, setting the macOS 15 floor.

**Changed**

- Set the **macOS 15.0** minimum, aligned with JackMate.
- First version stamp on the driver and the bundle.

**Added**

- A login LaunchAgent that hides the internal devices at boot.

## 0.8.0 — 2026-06-18 — Master, volume & sample rate

**Added**

- A **master box** (on/off) that replaces the plain monitor, with the system default output
  switched to the JackMoebius output at start.
- **Per-app volume** with a lockable *cadenas* (locked to the master by default).
- **Per-app input/output device-routing status** — the foundation for the correctness
  indicator.
- **Sample-rate matching:** the driver follows jackd's rate, across 12 advertised rates
  (8 kHz – 192 kHz).
- A clock-drift diagnostic gauge.

## 0.7.0 — 2026-06-16 — Bidirectional, per app

**Added**

- **Bidirectional per-app cards:** the daemon now receives from JACK, with a single box
  wiring **both directions** for each app, an input-card pool and allocator (`add` /
  `remove` / `clear --in`), and a masked card lifecycle.
- App detection on the live CoreAudio process list, unified input/output listings, and
  `--in` autocompletion.

**Changed**

- The forward device is split into a user-visible output device and a hidden internal tap.
- **JACK-tied visibility:** the internal devices are hidden, and capture is gated, while
  JACK is down.

## 0.6.0 — 2026-06-13 — Deterministic transport + the reverse device

**Added**

- The **reverse-path foundations:** an input (*In*) device, a reverse bus with a *Feed*
  write point, and a control-plane gate (the bus stays inert until claimed).

**Changed**

- **Deterministic bus transport** — a per-reader alignment delta on the write head removes
  the timing "anchor lottery" (later measured at ±26 ms per take).

## 0.5.0 — 2026-06-12 — Lifecycle & latency

**Added**

- Daemon lifecycle from the CLI (`start` / `stop` / `status`, clean SIGTERM).
- Exposure intents **persist** — boxes revive across daemon restarts.
- `clear` chains an implicit remove (unroute, drop the box, free the channels).
- Bridge latency computed and pushed to the driver, buffer tuning, monitor volume + mute.

## 0.4.0 — 2026-06-11 — One box per app

**Added**

- **SlotAllocator** — persistent, per-bundle-ID channel reservations (a saved patchbay
  restores itself).
- A HAL control plane with app-identity resolution.
- The **IPC server** and the **`jackmoebius` CLI**.
- **One JACK box per app** (localized names, a metadata tag, monitor control) with a
  lifecycle reconciler: a box is visible if and only if its app is running and exposed.

## 0.3.0 — 2026-06-11 — Into the JACK graph

**Added**

- **JackBridge** — monitor ports published in the JACK graph through a `dlopen`-ed libjack;
  the system mix becomes audible through JACK.
- A **supervised daemon** with auto-reconnect to both `jackd` and `coreaudiod`, plus latency
  instrumentation.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-06-11 — Continuous 64-channel capture

**Added**

- The **`jackmoebiusd`** daemon (a Swift package) with **AudioBridge** — continuous
  64-channel CoreAudio capture from the driver. Validated with live hot-routing and a
  10-minute endurance run.

## 0.1.0 — 2026-06-10 — The driver

The starting point was a close reading of [Stéphane Letz's note on moving *JackRouter* to
AudioServerPlugin](https://github.com/jackaudio/jack-router/blob/main/macOS/docs/JackRouter-AudioServerPlugin.md).
It lays out the showstoppers that turned the original JackRouter — built on the old
**AudioHardwarePlugin** HAL plug-in, broken since macOS 10.15 — into a dead end, and points
toward the modern **AudioServerPlugIn** driver model. JackMoebius doesn't follow that
proposal strictly, but several of its ideas set the direction.

**Added**

- The **AudioServerPlugIn driver** (Rust): a per-app virtual audio device exposing
  CoreAudio to a userspace plug-in.
- A 64-channel capture probe and a minimal HAL control tool.
- End-to-end validation of the full chain on modern macOS.
